introduction: These hundred readings use one of the oldest pictures there is. Guidance is light and its absence darkness; a lamp brought into a room shows everything at once; the heart is a glass and a niche; the Sun of Truth has risen and some prefer dark rooms; the friends are asked to be candles in a dark world and to fight no war but that of light against darkness. The readings also say that darkness has no existence of its own. Beside them stand Genesis and the Gospel of John, the Psalms and Isaiah, the Light Verse and the Qur’an's layers of darkness, the Dhammapada, Plato's cave and Milton's hymn to light. A few passages complicate the picture: Isaiah's God who creates darkness, the psalm for which night shines as day, Arnold's darkling plain, and the warning that the light in a person may itself be darkness.
questions: One reading says that when a lamp is brought into a room all things at once become visible, and such is the power of love. When has something like that happened in a room you were in?
The readings hold that darkness is only the absence of light; Isaiah has God say, I create darkness. Which account fits your experience of evil and ignorance?
Jesus warns that the light in a person may be darkness. How would someone discover that about themselves?
Plato's prisoners prefer the cave. Why do people resist a light that would show them more?
The readings speak of a war of light against darkness whose swords are words. What are the dangers of that language, and how do the readings guard against them?
Arnold saw a darkling plain, and one reading says the world is very dark. What sustains the confidence that the darkness of night is past?

outside.why: Isaiah says that the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
The first letter of John says that he that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and he that hateth his brother is in darkness.
The beloved in the Song of Songs says: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem.
Martin Luther King dreamed of a nation where his children would be judged not by the color of their skin but by the content of their character.
Plato said that as the sun is the author of visibility in visible things, so the good is the author of knowledge in things known.
The psalmist says to God: in Thy light shall we see light.
Jesus said that the light of the body is the eye, and if thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
The Light Verse of the Qur’an likens God's light to a niche wherein is a lamp, the lamp in a glass.
Jesus said: let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
Thoreau wrote that the light which puts out our eyes is darkness to us, and that only that day dawns to which we are awake. If the star is in every heart, what are the clouds?
Thoreau called the inventions of his day pretty toys, improved means to an unimproved end. What does a brilliantly lit city still lack?
Shakespeare's Portia says: how far that little candle throws his beams! So shines a good deed in a naughty world.
Jesus said that no man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light.
The psalm says: lo, children are an heritage of the Lord, as arrows in the hand of a mighty man.
The psalmist says to God: the darkness hideth not from Thee, but the night shineth as the day. If night and day are alike to God, what is darkness?
Socrates, freed from his chain, remarked how curiously pleasure is related to pain, which might be thought the opposite of it.
In Genesis God set lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night.
The Preacher saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
In Isaiah God says: I form the light, and create darkness; I make peace, and create evil. Is darkness only the absence of light, or something made?
Milton, blind, addressed the light he could no longer see: hail, holy Light, offspring of Heaven firstborn.
Malachi promises that the Sun of righteousness shall arise with healing in his wings.
The first letter of Peter speaks of a people called out of darkness into His marvellous light.
The psalmist says: Thou wilt light my candle; the Lord my God will enlighten my darkness.
Paul says that God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts.
The Letter to the Ephesians says: ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord.
The psalm calls the word of God a lamp unto the feet and a light unto the path.
Jesus warned: take heed therefore that the light which is in thee be not darkness. How can something a person takes for light be darkness?
Paul says that we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the power may be of God, and not of us.
From the cross Jesus prayed: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
John's Gospel says that men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
Plato imagined people chained from childhood in an underground den, facing away from the light. Why would anyone prefer a dark room and a candle to the sun?
The Qur’an says that God bringeth those who believe out of darkness into light.
Zacharias sings of the dayspring from on high, come to give light to them that sit in darkness.
Isaiah calls: arise, shine, for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
The Preacher says: truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun.
Isaiah says: woe unto them that put darkness for light, and light for darkness.
The Qur’an says that they would put out the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light.
John's Gospel says that the light shineth in darkness, and the darkness comprehended it not.
Habakkuk cries: O Lord, how long shall I cry, and Thou wilt not hear?

Matthew Arnold wrote that the world hath really neither joy, nor love, nor light, and that we are here as on a darkling plain where ignorant armies clash by night. What do you say to someone for whom the darkness is simply how things are?
The Dhammapada asks: why do you not seek a light, ye who are surrounded by darkness?
The psalmist says: the Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
Paul says: I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord.
The Letter to the Ephesians says that God, rich in mercy, hath quickened us together when we were dead.
The priestly blessing asks: the Lord make His face shine upon thee, and give thee peace.
The Qur’an swears by the morning hours and by the night when it is stillest: thy Lord hath not forsaken thee.
Micah says: when I sit in darkness, the Lord shall be a light unto me.
Paul hopes that his friends will shine as lights in the world, in the midst of a crooked generation.
Jesus said: I am the light of the world; he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness.
The Book of Daniel says that they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament.
In Genesis the first word spoken is a word about light: God said, Let there be light, and there was light.
The Qur’an says: light upon light; God guideth unto His light whom He will. Is the line between the people of light and the people of fire fixed, or crossed every day?
Paul says: let us cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light.
The Dhammapada says: this world is dark; few only can see here.
The psalmist says that the heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament sheweth His handiwork.
Isaiah hears: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.
Jesus told his followers: ye are the light of the world; a city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.
Paul speaks of a vail upon the heart that is taken away when the heart turns.
Jesus said that the Father maketh His sun to rise on the evil and on the good. If the sun shines on East and West alike, what keeps a place dark?
Amos told those who longed for the day of the Lord that it would be darkness, and not light. Is every claim that East and West have been illumined to be taken on trust?
Paul said that he was sent to open people's eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light.
The man healed in John's Gospel says: whereas I was blind, now I see.
The Qur’an asks whether he who was dead and was raised to life, with a light to walk by, is like one in utter darkness.
The psalm says that weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
The boy Samuel, called by name in the night, ran and answered: here am I.
Jesus said: while ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.
The psalm says that he that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
The psalmist says: bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits.
Paul tells the Thessalonians: ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day.
Isaiah says that the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light.
The Letter to the Ephesians says that we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers of the darkness of this world.
The same letter names the only sword: the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
Paul says that though we walk in the flesh, the weapons of our warfare are not carnal.
Jesus said: all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword. What are the risks of speaking about spiritual effort in the language of armies and war?
Paul asks the Romans to present their bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God.
Isaiah foresees nations beating their swords into plowshares, and learning war no more.
This is the image the reading recalls: the Qur’an speaks of darkness on a vast, abysmal sea, wave above wave, layer upon layer of darkness.
Yeats wrote after a great war: things fall apart; the centre cannot hold; mere anarchy is loosed upon the world. Can a few people be the cause of dispelling the darkness of an age?
Matthew's Gospel tells of wise men who came from the east, saying: we have seen his star.
At Pentecost tongues like as of fire sat upon each of the disciples, and they began to speak.
Proverbs says that the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.
Jesus said that men do not light a candle and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick.
Jesus said of John the Baptist: he was a burning and a shining light.
John's Gospel says of the Baptist: he was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light. What is the difference between giving light and bearing witness to it?
Macbeth says: out, out, brief candle; life's but a walking shadow. What answers the sense that one small life can light nothing?
George Eliot wrote that the growing good of the world is partly dependent on unhistoric acts.
The Book of Revelation says of the faithful dead that their works do follow them.
William Blake pictured the moment when the stars threw down their spears and watered heaven with their tears.
Blake wrote that we are put on earth a little space that we may learn to bear the beams of love.
Isaiah asks: who is among you that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? Let him trust in the name of the Lord.
Job speaks of a land of darkness and the shadow of death, where the light is as darkness. What can be said to someone for whom the world is this dark?
The psalmist prays: O send out Thy light and Thy truth; let them lead me.
The Qur’an teaches a prayer for refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak from the evil of the darkness when it is intense.
Paul asks: what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness, and what communion hath light with darkness?
When Jesus sat at meat with publicans and sinners, the Pharisees asked why. When is keeping apart from someone a protection, and when is it a failure to bring light where it is needed?
At the tomb Jesus cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth, and he that was dead came forth.
The Book of Revelation ends with a city of which it is said: there shall be no night there.
Isaiah calls to Zion: lift up thy voice with strength; say unto the cities of Judah, Behold your God.
Spinoza wrote that hatred is increased by being reciprocated, and can on the other hand be destroyed by love.
In the parable the wise virgins took oil in their vessels with their lamps.

psalm-darkness-and-light-both-alike.text: If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me. Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee

ecclesiastes-light-excelleth-darkness.text: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness. The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all

ephesians-sword-of-the-spirit.text: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God

john-epistle-hateth-his-brother-is-in-da.text: He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now. He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him. But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes

song-black-but-comely.text: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon

psalm-light-my-candle.text: For thou wilt light my candle: the Lord my God will enlighten my darkness

job-darkness-and-the-shadow-of-death.text: Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death; A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness

isaiah-walketh-in-darkness.text: Who is among you that feareth the Lord, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the Lord, and stay upon his God

acts-from-darkness-to-light.text: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me

luke-light-that-is-in-thee.text: Take heed therefore that the light which is in thee be not darkness

quran-by-the-morning-hours.text: By the morning hours And by the night when it is stillest, Thy Lord hath not forsaken thee nor doth He hate thee, And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former, And verily thy Lord will give unto thee so that thou wilt be content

quran-lord-of-the-daybreak.text: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak From the evil of that which He created; From the evil of the darkness when it is intense

dhammapada-this-world-is-dark.text: This world is dark, few only can see here; a few only go to heaven, like birds escaped from the net

dhammapada-seek-a-light.text: How is there laughter, how is there joy, as this world is always burning? Why do you not seek a light, ye who are surrounded by darkness

arnold-darkling-plain.text: for the world, which seems / To lie before us like a land of dreams, / So various, so beautiful, so new, / Hath really neither joy, nor love, nor light, / Nor certitude, nor peace, nor help for pain; / And we are here as on a darkling plain / Swept with confused alarms of struggle and flight, / Where ignorant armies clash by night
arnold-darkling-plain.author: Matthew Arnold
